Run the project's `## Test` blocks.

Discovers every `## Test: <prose name>` in the project, runs each in a fresh, isolated world on the interpreter tier, and prints a deterministic, name-ordered report. `Expect that` failures record-and-continue (one run reports everything); runaway tests fail at a deterministic op budget (the timeout that cannot flake); skips are loud, need a reason, and fail the run unless budgeted under `[test] skip_budget` in Largo.toml.

Usage: largo test [OPTIONS] [FILTER]

Arguments:
  [FILTER]
          Run only tests whose prose name contains this substring

Options:
      --seed <SEED>
          The suite seed (default 0 — reproducibility is the default)
          
          [default: 0]

      --format <FORMAT>
          Report format
          
          [default: text]
          [possible values: text, json]

      --json
          Emit the machine-readable CLAIM INVENTORY as JSON: every `## Test` classified by kind (example / finite-enumeration property) with an honest status, vacuous flags, disclosed domain bounds, and any concrete counterexample. A superset of `--format json`

      --live
          Also run capability-granted tests (`This test may use the real filesystem.` etc.) — they leave the hermetic no-flake guarantee

      --prove
          Escalate finite-domain `For all` properties to exhaustive proof (booleans are checked over every case, not sampled) → rank PROVEN

      --tiers <TIERS>
          Cross-tier differential: `all` (or a list of `interpreter`,`vm`) also runs each passing test's computation on the bytecode VM and compares it byte for byte, failing if the compiled tier cannot run what the interpreter did (the F18 "works-on-my-tier" guard). Any other value is refused rather than ignored

      --browser
          A mounted test's page tiers also drive a real headless Chrome (`CHROME_BIN`, or the first of `google-chrome`/`google-chrome-stable`/`chromium`/`chromium-browser`/`chrome` on `PATH`) and must agree with it, exactly as they already must agree with the lowered bytecode VM. No Chrome found is a refused run, not a silent skip

  -q, --quiet
          Suppress informational output (errors still print)

  -v, --verbose...
          Increase output verbosity (repeatable)

      --color <WHEN>
          When to use terminal colors

          Possible values:
          - auto:   Color when stdout/stderr is a terminal and `NO_COLOR` is unset
          - always: Always emit ANSI, even into pipes (CI logs, `less -R`)
          - never:  Never emit ANSI
          
          [default: auto]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Examples:
  largo test
  largo test withdraw
  largo test --seed 7
  largo test --format json
  largo test --json
